title: MTC continues to knock it out of the park with their programming!  Re...
transcript: The Balusters might just be my favorite play currently on Broadway. It is by playwright David Lindsay-Abaire, most recently known for his work on Kimberly Akimbo, and satirizes the hypocrisy that exists in a lot of wealthy communities that present themselves as, and believe themselves to be, incredibly Liberal and progressive. It covers several meetings of a wealthy neighborhood association discussing various topics concerning the neighborhood. This includes everything from a serial package thief to what railings (or balusters) a house is allowed to install on their porch, and most pivotally, whether or not to install a stop sign onto a busy intersection at the expense of the visual appeal of the town's main street. And while a lot of those conversations probably sound quite boring, I assure you the play is actually incredibly funny. In fact, it is probably the funniest play of the season. And it is within these conversations that we actually learn a lot about these characters, as it isn't really about the stop sign or the balusters, and more about what those things represent. With the balusters representing this clash between tradition and modernity, and the stop sign representing safety versus aesthetics. And of course, there are a ton of internal politics at play as well, all of which is designed to make the audience question if this seemingly diverse community of people is actually as inclusive and progressive as it claims to be. And this is brought to life by a really stellar Ensemble of actors led by Anika Noni Rose. But the standout is definitely Marylouise Burke as penny, the older woman of the group. She got a well deserved Tony nomination for this show, as did Richard Thomas as the association's longtime president and neighborhood realtor, who serves as the old guard to Anika Noni Rose's new guard. I also have to shout out the stunning set by Derek McLane. I think it is one of the major snubs of the season that it was not nominated for the Tony. but the overall production itself was nominated for 5 Tonys, including best play. And as I said, it might just be my favorite play on Broadway right now, so Balusters is going to get a very strong Broadway Ben Recommendation.
